No.20

Are Natural Disasters and Human Calamities Predestined?

Before disaster and impermanence, turning from fear of karmic results to the causes that can still be changed.

Author's record · translated; the Chinese original is authoritative

Open in reading mode →

🔶Inquiry to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva

I asked the Bodhisattva to teach: are natural disasters and human calamities predestined?

🔶The Bodhisattva's Teaching

"Karma has fixed results,
and also conditions that can turn."
"The shared karma of beings
forms their mountains and rivers;
individual karma ripens
when its season comes."
"It cannot be changed by a single thought,
nor is it wholly unchangeable."

"To know causes and understand effects
is not for fear,
but for awakening."

🔶Plain Rendering

Karma has results that will surely appear,
and also conditions that can be changed.
▎Disasters in the wider world (such as earthquakes and epidemics)
are "shared karma".
▎Misfortunes a person meets (such as car accidents and other accidents)
are "individual karma" ripening at that moment.
They cannot be changed by a single thought,
nor are they completely unchangeable.

Knowing how cause and effect work
is not meant to make you afraid of retribution,
but to help you live with more understanding.

🔶Inquiry to Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva

I replied to the Bodhisattva: could the Bodhisattva explain in more detail, "To know causes and understand effects is not for fear, but for awakening"?

🔶The Bodhisattva's Teaching

"To know causes and understand effects
is not to make the heart afraid,
but to make the heart clear."
"The fearful see the effect and retreat;
the awakened see the cause and turn."
"To practice out of dread of retribution
is to avoid suffering;
to act from understanding
is to leave suffering behind."

"Those who understand causes gain freedom;
those who fear effects are forever bound."

🔶Plain Rendering

"Knowing the principle of cause and effect is not meant to make your heart afraid, but to make your heart clear."

"Fearful people shrink back only when they see the result (a bad outcome); awakened people begin to change as soon as they see the cause (the arising of an intention)."

"If you practice only because you fear retribution, you are running from suffering; if you practice because you understand the principle, you are walking toward liberation."

"Those who understand cause and effect gain freedom; those who fear results are bound forever."
